verdict_input_note: The task input carried the transport verdict in full but was truncated before the terminal and admission verdicts. Their findings were reconstructed from the verifiers' own probe scripts, which were re-run against the delivered sources; every reconstructed finding is listed with the judgement made.
not_implemented_exactly: Hidden second pass (lead decision): the contract allows "account for or disable"; the capture disables it (one send per query attempt). A server 400 that would trigger litellm's pass 2 then reaches the caller as litellm's mapping of the refusal (InternalServerError), not as a success after pass 2. The server's own status and error are kept in the outcome record and every such case is reported in integrity().frozen_path_parity and the episode record; it does NOT stop the queue. Whether it should is for the lead.

Diagnostic hand-off margin: to keep the cleanup reserve at least 90 s including the supervisor's own post-kill confirmation, the diagnostic deadline is min(start + 30 s, absolute cleanup deadline - 90 s - 4 s). The per-command timeout is the contract formula applied to that deadline. This is stricter than the stated formula, never looser.

Host reserve: no repository source declares the existing host disk reserve. The episode requires it as --host-reserve-bytes and records it; the fixtures used 1 GiB. The lead or launcher must set the live value.
Live host/server step: not implemented. cue_episode.run_assignment raises LiveReleaseHeld and cue_runner offers only --dry-run/--validate; episode_argv shows the launch line a live runner would use.

Process-group limit: a host-side descendant that calls setsid leaves the group and cannot be killed by group signals; it is detected only while it holds the output pipe. The docker exec client does not do this, and in-container processes end with the container cleanup that always follows.

SDK binding scope: the 20 files on the traced request path are byte-verified against their RECORD digests, and each of the five distributions' RECORD is bound; other installed files are pinned through RECORD only, not re-hashed.

Interpreters: pytest runs in the project interpreter; the pinned interpreter has no pytest and was not modified, so every pinned-SDK part runs there through subprocess (the transport SDK fixture and the integration harness).

Logical ids: the driver opens the logical id before the frozen request_timeout pre-check (the frozen AccountedModel increments after it), so a query refused by the deadline still consumes an id and gets an explicit incomplete record; ids then equal the agent's n_calls. No model-visible effect.

Cue form: the cue is appended as one user message at the end of the model-visible history before the delivery query, and stays in the history of later calls (the form used by the transport fixture). The lead text fixes the cue and its timing, not the message role or position; the lead should confirm this form.

Accepted pins: workspace_capture.py and pilot_report.py are checked against the worker-published docs/req005_fixture_landmarks_20260923.json because the lead audit lists no digest for them; the lead may prefer to add them to its audit.
Start preflight: both the private and the public receipt directories must each show at least the reserve + 6 GiB free (conservative when they are on different devices).

Tamper evidence is local: the head file detects a truncated ledger and the launch marker a deleted namespace, but an operator who deliberately rewrites both can defeat them; the published git history remains the external anchor.

Request accounting: the episode reports its physical requests from the capture (the authoritative send ledger); the runner-side AssignmentRequestBudget is not consumed per send across the process boundary, and the per-episode cap is enforced in-process by the transport budget min(48, 576 - counted).

SIGALRM through the full driver: the frozen one-shot alarm path is reused unchanged and the capture's deadline handling is tested with a real SIGALRM at unit level; no integrated episode was driven into its inference deadline (timing-dependent).

mutation_survey.method: worker-run, deterministic: each mutant is one single-site source edit applied to a scratch copy of experiments/, then the component test file is run with pytest -x (the transport file includes its pinned-SDK subprocess fixtures). KILLED means at least one test failed. Worker-reported, not independently verified

equivalent_mutants.reason: drops the probe_error conjunct of the start preflight; when a probe raises, its observed value stays None, so the remaining conjuncts already fail the preflight: the mutant is logically equivalent. The verifier's original M23 (a raising probe passing) is refused by test_the_start_preflight_refuses_an_unmeasurable_disk_and_probes_both_directories
